This selloff in memory stocks makes absolutely NO sense to me.

$MU, $SNDK, Samsung and SK Hynix are getting hit after China's CXMT announced progress on its new 4F² DRAM architecture, with plans to introduce DDR5 server memory using the technology by the end of 2026. For those unfamiliar, this technology is designed to pack more memory cells into the same amount of space, potentially improving chip density and manufacturing efficiency.

Now, I want to make something clear. CXMT is absolutely becoming a legitimate competitor because acording to TrendForce, CXMT has already captured roughly 9.5% of global DRAM revenue, up from 7.6% the previous quarter, making it the fourth largest DRAM manufacturer globally. The company is also expanding aggressively, with new manufacturing facilities in Shanghai and Hefei targeting more than 600,000 wafers per month, potentially doubling its manufacturing capacity. On top of that, CXMT has reportedly started mass production of its G5 DRAM platform and LPDDR6 memory, while its new 4F² architecture could make memory production even more efficient.

But here's why I think the market is getting WAY ahead of itself. First, announcing a new memory architecture and successfully manufacturing it at scale are two completely different things. CXMT still needs to prove it can deliver competitive yields, pricing, reliability, and production volumes. Second, we're currently dealing with an enormous memory supply shortage, particularly as hyperscalers continue increasing AI infrastructure spending. Even if CXMT successfully doubles its capacity, that doesn't automatically mean the industry becomes oversupplied. Demand for memory is expected to grow substantially over the next several years, and we're already seeing manufacturers secure longer term supply agreements with customers.

Third, this announcement is primarily focused on conventional DDR5 server memory, NOT HBM. That's an important distinction because HBM is becoming one of the most valuable parts of the memory industry, with Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix benefiting from enormous AI demand. And SanDisk primarily manufactures NAND flash memory, not DRAM. So selling $SNDK specifically because of a DDR5 technology announcement seems even more questionable. Now, that doesn't mean CXMT won't eventually put pressure on conventional DRAM prices. Increased Chinese manufacturing capacity is absolutely something investors should monitor, especially over the longer term but I think investors are confusing a legitimate long term competitive threat with an immediate change in industry fundamentals. Nothing about today's announcement suddenly creates millions of additional memory chips, eliminates existing supply shortages, or changes the amount of memory needed to power AI infrastructure. I've been saying this for months. The amount of memory we're going to need over the next decade is INSANE. When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example. 

SpaceX is a rare counter-example, where its mass to orbit is roughly an order of magnitude greater than the rest of the world, BUT China now does a majority of non-SpaceX mass to orbit. SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix. 

Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low margin commodity only ~3 years ago. LP5 and LP6 are designed to a common standard that China seems to be solving fast. 

Newer HBM architectures and things like an SRAM layer below logic and 3D stacking RAM on top of logic while finding a way to keep the logic cooled will be harder to solve.

有人把 Switch 版暗黑2重制版搬上了 iPhone，开源免费，游戏得你自己出

GitHub 上一个叫 D2R Mobile 的开源项目，能把你自己买的 Switch 版《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》（暗黑2重制版）连同“术士君临”资料片装到 iPhone 和 iPad 上离线玩。项目用 MIT 许可证开源，代码免费，仓库里不含任何游戏内容。暗黑2重制版官方只有电脑和游戏主机版本，“术士君临”是今年初推出的资料片，新增了术士职业。

【它怎么做到的】

iPhone 和 Switch 用的是同一类 ARM 处理器，能执行同一套机器指令。所以这个项目没走模拟器的路子，Switch 版游戏的原程序直接在手机处理器上运行，只改写了极少数在苹果系统下不能原样执行的指令（涉及线程寄存器、系统调用和计时器），作者说其余部分逐字节保持原样。

游戏需要的系统服务，由一个专为苹果平台写的小程序提供。画面部分在苹果的图形接口 Metal 上重新实现，着色器（负责画面渲染的小程序）从游戏原版提前翻译好。模拟器要在游戏和硬件之间加一层实时翻译，这里没有这一层。因为跑的就是原版程序，职业、符文之语、掉落规则、任务流程都和原版一样。

【想玩要准备什么】

设备是 iOS 26 及以上的 iPhone 或 iPad，两者共用一个安装包。

游戏要正版 Switch 版本体加“术士君临”资料片，并更新到 3.3.94012 版本。作者说没有资料片的版本不支持，也没测过。

游戏文件要从你自己的主机里取出来，要哪些、怎么取、放在哪，项目单独写了一篇文档。这一步对普通玩家有门槛。

还需要一个 Apple 账号给 App 签名。付费开发者账号功能最全；免费 Apple ID 也能用，但没有 iCloud 存档同步，每 7 天要重新签名安装一次。

仓库里没有游戏程序、美术、文字和数据表，这些都在你自己的电脑上用你自己的文件现做出来。项目声明与暴雪、任天堂没有关联，也没有得到它们的认可，只能配合自己拥有的正版游戏使用。游戏完全离线，不支持联机，不需要登录任何账号。

【怎么装】

有 Apple 芯片的 Mac 并装了 Xcode，是作者主推的路线：把游戏文件放进指定目录，运行准备脚本（检查工具、改写程序、翻译着色器），填好签名信息，构建出 App 装到手机上。准备脚本第一次跑耗时较长。

没有 Mac，可以从项目发布页下载一个不含游戏内容的“空壳”安装包，在 Windows 上用项目的工具把自己的游戏内容做进去，再用 Sideloadly、AltStore 这类自签工具签名装机。这条路的手机第一次启动要花约 7 分钟编译着色器，只有这一次。作者说 Windows 上从做包到真机游玩已经走通，用自签工具签名这一步还在等用户反馈，Linux 上做包也没验证过。

装好第一次打开，App 会让你选“游戏资源文件夹”。安装包本身一百多 MB，游戏资源约 5.6GB 另放进手机，以后升级 App 不动存档和资源。

【玩起来怎么样】

下面的数字都来自作者在项目页上的自述，目前没有第三方测试。

作者说，内测用了 44 台 iPhone 和 iPad，全部完成了普通、噩梦、地狱三个难度的多角色通关。最低实测机型是 iPhone 14 Pro Max（A16 芯片，6GB 内存），能跑满 60 帧。

在 iPhone 17 Pro Max 上，作者测得局内稳定 60 帧，从主菜单进游戏约 1 秒。60 帧时整机功耗约 3.8 瓦，按电池容量换算能连续玩近 5 小时；省电模式降到 30 帧，功耗约 1.85 瓦，续航约翻倍。功耗是在第一幕营地站着、亮度 50% 时测的，续航是换算出来的，并非实际从满电玩到没电。

操作按触屏重新设计：摇杆移动，点地面或 NPC 自动寻路，技能按钮按住连放、拖动可朝任意方向瞄准，双击装备直接穿脱，长按背包空格自动整理。接上手柄会切换到原版的手柄界面，键位和 Switch 一致。整个游戏可以在中文和英文之间切换。

【原版没有的东西】

项目在原版之上加了一套终局内容：通关地狱后开放的 100 层“秘境”，12 关的首领连战，以及建角色时可选的“极乐世界”模式，暗金、套装、符文掉率大幅提高。

便利功能有自动喝药（佣兵也会自动喂药）、低级符文和宝石自动拾取、高价值掉落时手机震动提醒、免费鉴定和回城，仓库也扩大了。多数功能可以在游戏设置里逐项开关。

目前只支持 iPhone 和 iPad。作者说安卓手机用的是同一类处理器，这套做法可以照搬，要换的只是系统服务和图形对接那一层，但作者手边没有安卓手机，希望有人接手。

项目地址：https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile

Meta 发布 Muse Wonder：开发者今天能用，普通用户还要等

Meta 10 月 12 日发布新一代大模型 Muse Wonder，一共两个版本：Muse Wonder 主打速度，Muse Wonder Full 是完整版。扎克伯格说，这个模型让 Meta 进入了“前沿”梯队，也就是和 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 最强模型同一档。

做这个模型的是 Meta 超级智能实验室（Meta Superintelligence Labs）。按 Meta 的说法，14 个月前它把 AI 业务推倒重来，从底层技术栈重新搭起，第一代成果是 Muse Spark 系列。Muse Wonder 比 Muse Spark 大得多，在 Meta 吉瓦级的 Prometheus 数据中心训练。

【谁能用，怎么用】

开发者今天就能用 Muse Wonder：通过 Meta Model API（Meta 的大模型接口平台）调用，或者在 Meta 的 AI 编程工具 Muse Code 里用。

完整版 Muse Wonder Full 目前只开放给 Muse Code 的订阅用户。官方博客只写了它在 Muse Code 里可用，没提 API。

普通用户用的 AI 助手 Muse，官方博客写的是“很快”接入 Muse Wonder，先给订阅用户。扎克伯格在 X 上说的是“今天订阅就能用 Muse Wonder 驱动你的 Muse”，两边说法有出入。免费用户什么时候能用，Meta 只说会逐步把这个水平的能力带给所有人，以后还会用 Muse Wonder 开发专门的模型给所有 Muse 用户，没给时间表。

模型卡写的规格：上下文 100 万 Token，够一次放进一个中大型代码仓库；能读文字、图片、视频和音频，输出只有文字。

【和 Claude、GPT 比怎么样】

下面的成绩都来自 Meta 自己公布的对比表，对手是 Claude Opus 5.5、Claude Fable 5.1 和 GPT-6 Astra，全部按最高推理强度测。其中个人超级智能指数、MemoryBench、FocusBench 是 Meta 自建的测试。对手的成绩有一部分是 Meta 自己跑的，模型卡也写明，这些跑法未必为对手模型调到了最优。

Muse Wonder Full 领先的主要是三类任务。

一是替人办事的智能体任务。Meta 自建的个人超级智能指数，Muse Wonder Full 59.1 分，Claude Opus 5.5 55.2，GPT-6 Astra 54.5；跑完整业务流程的 AutomationBench，45.4 对对手最高的 41.6。

二是长时间写代码。DeepSWE 79.0，对手最高 74.2；做大型软件项目的 SWE-Marathon 57.5，对手最高 46.3。

三是法律。法律 AI 公司 Harvey 的智能体测试 13.1，对手最高 8.6。这个测试要求交付物每一项都达标，所有模型的通过率都很低。

落后的项目也不少，大多输给 Claude Opus 5.5：终端编程（Terminal-Bench）57.1 对 59.6，从零写一个完整程序（ProgramBench）59.0 对 70.5，操作电脑（OSWorld）78.4 对 81.8，健康问答 62.3 对 65.6。专业文档任务 GDP.pdf 输给 GPT-6 Astra，33.2 对 34.2。

Meta 博客里也放了第三方机构 Artificial Analysis 的综合智能指数：Claude Opus 5.5 以 58 分排第一，Muse Wonder Full 56 分排第二。开发者现在能通过 API 调用的是 Muse Wonder，它是 52 分，低于 Claude Fable 5.1、GPT-6 Astra 和 Google 的 Gemini 4 Argon（都是 53 分）。

按 Meta 给的数据，让 AI 长时间替你干活、跨对话记住你的情况，是 Muse Wonder 领先的地方；比综合能力，它还排在 Claude Opus 5.5 后面。

【Active Memory 和 Active Focus 是什么】

这是 Meta 给两项能力起的名字，也是这次发布的卖点。

Active Memory（主动记忆）：跨对话记住和你有关的重要信息，做新任务时自己判断哪些旧信息用得上，主动调出来。Meta 用自建的 MemoryBench 测这项能力：在 6.4 万到 10 万 Token 的长对话里掺进干扰内容，还有和前文矛盾、后来又更新的信息，看模型最后能不能记对关键细节。Muse Wonder 85.6 分，Muse Wonder Full 85.5，Claude Opus 5.5 81.5。

Active Focus（主动专注）：盯着一个难目标持续干下去，一条路走不通就换一条，遇到卡点自己想办法，情况变了跟着调整；需要时会问你，做重要操作前先跟你确认。Meta 用自建的 FocusBench 测这项能力，任务涉及租房、旅行、IT、理财等，模型要在多轮交互里应付各种现实障碍。

Meta 的演示里，Muse Wonder 直接在浏览器和多个 App 之间操作，根据用户的个人偏好和情况排出一份周六跑步计划。

【官方没说的】

价格：博客和模型卡都没写 API 怎么收费，也没写 Muse、Muse Code 的订阅多少钱。

开源：没说会不会开放模型权重。模型卡只提到，开发和部署期间按 Meta 的权重安全计划保护模型权重。Meta 过去的 Llama 系列是开放权重的，这次没有任何相关说法。

安全：Meta 说这一代模型防范化学、生物、放射性、核武器和网络攻击滥用的措施是它迄今最强的，同时保留了用于网络防御的能力。完整的安全评估报告“很快”发布。

a16z's Martin Casado with http://MakerMaker.AI CTO Owen He on why a lot of RSI pitches are selling something as old as the steam engine:

Martin: "I see a lot of pitches come in, and a lot of them use the term RSI. And I'll be like, 'Oh, so what do you do?' And they'll say, 'We use AI to create AI.' 'That sounds very interesting. So what do you do?' 'We use AI to create GPU kernels.'"

Owen: "RSI is definitely an overloaded term today... The important thing when you are differentiating them is to ask the question, what is the optimizer and what is the optimizee? When you're self-improving, who is improving?"

"There are people who are saying, 'Okay, we're doing RSI. We have humans using AI to develop better AI.' But that to us is just autocatalysis... the ideas and the improvement come from human brains."

Martin: "Most technical epochs have had autocatalytic effects. There's no way you can create a computer chip without a computer... You could build better steam engines because you could get coal faster, etc. So this notion of using the thing to build the thing faster is not new."

Owen: "That human brain was never the optimizee. Now, for the first time, we could swap the optimizer as the optimizee... The brain of the agents, which is the LLM, the model, can be the thing that you're optimizing, and this leads to this reinvestment of cognitive improvement into itself."

http://MakerMaker.AI co-founders Dhaval Adjodah and Owen He with a16z's Martin Casado on recursive self-improvement, and how to tell when it's real:

A lot of RSI pitches are really just people using AI to build better AI. Tech has always worked that way. You needed computers to build chips. Steam engines got better once you could get coal faster.

Dhaval and Owen's bar is higher. The model has to improve itself: its weights, its harness, even the prompt that tells it what to work on next.

And the gains have to hold up when you count what they cost. They track everyone's experiment spend on a "bleeder board," and one engineer, the Viceroy of Variance, has the job of breaking their results.

Over the past few months, they've started seeing early signs of their system getting better and cheaper at the same time.

http://MakerMaker.AI CEO Dhaval Adjodah and CTO Owen He on building a self-improving AI company where humans and agents work as one system:

"One big limit of [RSI] is the human element. I think the way that a lot of AI companies are thinking is, let us use AI to replace humans."

"But what we found is that there's so much that good researchers and good engineers can bring to the table that's gonna be very hard to replace by agents."

"And so that's why from the very beginning, we've tried to think of our basically entire company as a multi-agent system, where humans are a kind of agent that's cohabitating with other AI agents."

"We have one of our engineers that we named the Viceroy of Variance. That's a real thing. His job is to go and destroy the results we have and find what's wrong."

"So far we have not found a replacement for what we call quality time. Literally running hundreds of experiments, looking at it, developing an intuition, trying to figure out what is wrong, what is not wrong... what is just variance, what is not."
